hypothesis: Training-only corruption of pixels at known source corners may improve masked-input localization while preserving clean lower-front detection and endpoint accuracy. No improvement is assumed.
recipe_identity_scope: The recipe ID/hash describe the unchanged base numerical trainer settings. This protocol and each receipt additionally bind the experimental role and input-corruption specification.

target_contract.name: known-source-geometry-under-pixel-corruption-v1
target_contract.source_files: All canonical image and label files remain byte-identical. Both experimental roles use the exact PR35 annotation composition.
target_contract.boxes: Retain the transformed pre-corruption source-visible-front box. It is a reconstruction target, not a newly measured visible extent or full amodal object box.
target_contract.keypoints: Retain all transformed known source coordinates and flags; source v2 denotes observation before corruption. Never create coordinates for source v0 slots.
target_contract.score: Learned endpoint availability under this supervision; not an independently calibrated physical-visibility probability.
target_contract.validation: Only training preprocess receives the transform. Validation and evaluation input pixels stay unchanged unless explicitly part of the separately fixed PR60 diagnostic.

synthetic_probe.scope: Reused development regression probe; these scenes and failures informed the hypothesis. Not an untouched test.

decision.failure_decision: Retain PR35; no threshold, seed, epoch, radius or target-subset search to manufacture acceptance.
decision.interpretation: Prospective practical minimum for a development candidate, not a statistical-significance or deployment claim.

limits: One seed and one matched pair; finalize epoch30 for both.
The 137/20 split and source labels remain fixed; revised development references are for post-training evaluation only.
No naturally hidden corner is filled with a model or geometric guess.
Synthetic masking exposure, skipped attempts and collateral known coordinates must be reported.
Natural hidden-corner error remains unknown where independent coordinates do not exist.
Independent representative scenes and an application acceptance contract remain necessary for deployment readiness.
